Rebuild this interaction 1:1: Methods' payout slider - drag the handle across a waveform bar graph and the monthly goal amount updates live from $100 to $10,000+.

## Integration
Integration: stack-agnostic spec - springs given as stiffness/damping, timed motions as duration + curve; map every value to your framework and animation library of choice.

## Scene
A light onboarding screen: back chevron, slim progress bar, the question "How much do you want to make this month?" with "Set your desired payout amount" beneath, a huge dollar amount centered, a waveform-style slider (many thin vertical bars like an audio wave) with a purple dot handle, and a pink-purple Continue button.

## Motion spec
Pattern: waveform slider with a scaling bar graph and live amount readout.
- The waveform bars left of the handle are filled purple; right of it, gray - the fill boundary tracks the handle 1:1 while dragging.
- Bars near the handle scale up (height +40% easing off over ~6 bars) so the wave bulges around the touch point - the graph feels physical.
- The big amount updates live with the drag (no lag, no debounce), snapping to round steps ($100 increments under $1,000, larger steps above); at the max it flips to "$10,000+" with a small scale bump (1 -> 1.06 -> 1, 200ms).
- On release the handle settles with a tiny spring (~380/18) to the nearest step; haptic tick per step while dragging.
- Continue stays enabled at every value - the slider is a preference, not a gate.

## Calibration
- The amount's font size holds constant across $100 and $10,000+ - the layout never jumps, the text just changes.
- The wave bulge follows the finger, not the value - moving slowly keeps the bulge under the touch.

## Reduced motion
Fill boundary updates without the bar bulge; amount updates without the bump.

## Don't miss
- The slider is the waveform itself - there is no separate track line; the bars are the control.
- $10,000+ is a distinct cap state (the "+"), not just a big number.
